notes.title: Drawing Cards in Dino Citadel – But Not Like You’re Used To
notes.notes: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45314301/837b7550afbeba657ff23e09f1b330b05bef7b56.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Hey everyone![/b][/p][p]Today I want to talk about one of the core systems in [b]Dino Citadel[/b] — something that defines the entire flow of combat and decision-making: [b]how you draw cards[/b].[/p][p]In most deckbuilders, it’s simple. At the start of your turn, you automatically draw a hand of cards — maybe five. You play some, ignore others, and at the end of the turn, they all slide into your discard pile.[/p][p]But in [b]Dino Citadel[/b], there’s no auto-draw. At least, not the way you’re used to.[/p][p]Instead, you [b]spend Coin to add cards to your hand[/b], one by one. Every card is a decision. Every Coin is a choice. And your hand? You build it — you don’t just receive it.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]The [b]Order Pile[/b] is Dino Citadel’s version of the draw pile, but with a twist.[/p][p]At the start of each [b]Shard[/b] (closed-off regions with specific objectives), your deck is shuffled into the Order Pile. Then, at the start of each turn, you draw 3 cards from it — but they don’t go to your hand yet.[/p][p]To actually play one, you must [b]spend Coin to buy it[/b] and add it to your hand. The rest go to the discard pile… unless you intervene.[/p][p]You have a few tools:[/p][list][*][p][b]Freeze:[/b] You can freeze 1 card each turn. Frozen cards stay as an option for the next turn, giving you another chance to buy them.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Reroll:[/b] If you don’t like your 3 options, you can spend Coin to reroll. All unfrozen cards are discarded, and you draw new ones — letting you buy another card if you want.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Free cards:[/b] Some cards, especially [b]Bounty cards[/b], cost 0 Coin and go straight to your hand when drawn.[/p][/*][/list][p]Even once a card is in your hand, it still costs [b]Energy[/b] to play it. So each turn becomes a three-part decision tree:[/p][list][*][p]What can I afford to [b]buy[/b]?[/p][/*][*][p]What can I afford to [b]play[/b]?[/p][/*][*][p]What should I [b]save[/b] for next turn?[/p][/*][/list][p]This system turns every turn into a small, evolving puzzle — where you’re not just reacting to what’s drawn, but shaping what your future turns can become.[/p][p]You’re not handed a hand. You build it — one decision at a time.[/p][p][b]And Yes — It All Loops Back. [/b]Like most deckbuilders, once your Order Pile is empty, your discard pile is reshuffled and recycled.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Why This System Exists[/b][/h3][p][b]Dino Citadel[/b] isn’t just a deckbuilder. It’s also a game about [b]resource management[/b].[/p][p]Here’s the core loop:  [/p][list][*][p]Use [b]free Bounty cards[/b] to interact with the map and earn Coin[/p][/*][*][p]Spend that [b]Coin[/b] to buy tactical cards from the Order Pile[/p][/*][*][p]Spend [b]Energy[/b] to play those cards and survive[/p][/*][/list][p]Your economy is your draw engine.[/p][p]So you’ll need to:[/p][list][*][p]Use Bounty cards to gather resources[/p][/*][*][p]Use purchased cards to protect them, attack, or reposition[/p][/*][*][p]Carefully manage your Coin between buying, rerolling, and long-term planning[/p][/*][/list][p]Take the card [b]Harvester[/b], for example. It’s a free card that places a unit on a productive land tile. That Harvester will passively generate Coin or Food every turn — but only if it survives.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45314301/8c2c3e2afbf1b526d7fad9646044950cb2baff7c.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p]That’s it for drawing cards in [b]Dino Citadel[/b]![/p][p]If you enjoyed this peek behind the curtain, please consider wishlisting[b] [/b]and following[b] Dino Citadel[/b] on Steam.[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3352930/Dino_Citadel/"][/dynamiclink] [/p][p]Thanks for reading![/p][p][b]Halit[/b] [/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Thank You + Demo News
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45314301/b666dbf085e9c04e7f03b773ea2b16082848a79a.png"][/img][b]Hey everyone,[/b][/p][p] I just wanted to say a quick thank you to all the new people who’ve wishlisted [b]Dino Citadel[/b] lately. I see every single one, and it really means a lot. I’m just one person making this weird little game about a dinosaur carrying a castle through a corrupted world, and knowing people are curious enough to wishlist it really gives me fuel.[/p][p][b]
📢 Now for some real news:[/b][/p][p]The demo is coming in [b]November 2025[/b].[/p][p]It’ll cover the first steps into the [b]expanse[/b], the game’s larger world made up of shattered zones called [b]shards[/b]. You’ll get to experience the full core loop: buying cards, playing commands, moving across the grid, managing food and energy, and even rescuing your first corrupted[b] kin[/b], called [b]Moonfang[/b], if you manage to survive as things fall apart around you.[/p][p]I’m working hard to make sure the demo feels like a true part of the full game. Not just a teaser, but a real shard of the full experience.[/p][p][b]
🧭 What’s next?[/b][/p][p]We’ll be doing a playtest ahead of the demo. I’ll also share more detailed posts soon, including a closer look at the demo content and how the playtest will work. If you’re curious, keep an eye out or follow the game to stay in the loop. [/p][p]
✅ [b]In the meantime:[/b][/p][p]• Wishlist the game if you haven’t already. It helps a lot[/p][p]• Follow the game for updates, dev posts, and discussions[/p][p]• Follow me on [url="https://bsky.app/profile/heghy.bsky.social"]Bluesky[/url] for updates and ramblings[/p][p]• Or just check back in later. I’ll be here, building[/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3352930/Dino_Citadel/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]Thanks again. Really.[/p][p]Halit [i](developer of Dino Citadel)[/i][/p]
